title: Purposes of criminal law
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:33Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point covers only the purposes of punishment (deterrence, retribution, rehabilitation, incapacitation, denunciation), while the new point is about the broader purposes of criminal law, including protecting people and property and setting standards of behaviour, which the bank point does not teach.

draft.title: Purposes of criminal law
card: Criminal law deals with conduct that harms individuals or the community as a whole. The state, not the victim, brings the case against the accused.
it protects people and property from harm, such as assault, theft and damage.
it sets out the behaviour the community expects, by making some conduct a crime.
it allows courts to punish those found guilty, which can also discourage others from offending.
draft.remember: Criminal law protects, sets standards and allows punishment.

a.q: Parliament makes it a crime to carry a knife in a public place without a good reason. Which purpose of criminal law does this show most clearly?
opts: Setting standards of behaviour in the community
Allowing a victim to claim money for loss
Punishing a person who has already been found guilty
Settling a dispute between two neighbours
a.why: Making conduct a crime tells the community what behaviour is expected. It is not about punishing a particular person yet, and the state, not a victim, enforces criminal law.
a.clue: Think about what the rule tells everyone before anyone breaks it.

b.q: Priya is found guilty of stealing a bicycle from a shop in Ballarat, and the court orders a penalty. Which purpose is the court mainly carrying out?
opts: Allowing punishment of a person who broke the law
Protecting property by making theft a crime
Setting the standard that theft is wrong
Helping the shop owner recover the bicycle's value
b.why: The court is dealing with a person already found guilty, so it is using its power to punish. Protecting property and setting standards are served by the law itself, before any case reaches court.
b.clue: Look at the stage of the case: guilt has already been decided.

a.best: Setting standards of behaviour in the community

b.best: Allowing punishment of a person who broke the law
